text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.56% today to $422.50, building on a sharp 6.8% gain over the past two trading days. The immediate catalyst appears to be oil price strength: crude jumped from around $95 to $96.16 per barrel even as the G7 announced plans to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months. That counterintuitive move—oil prices holding firm despite a large reserve release—likely signals market concern that geopolitical risks (escalating U.S.-Iran tensions, ongoing Middle East conflict) outweigh the supply boost, supporting refinery margins and fuel demand.

The broader backdrop also supports refiners: U.S. refineries are running at 92.5% capacity utilization, and diesel inventories remain relatively tight at 105 million barrels despite the G7's imminent release. This combination of tight near-term supply and strong crude prices typically benefits Marathon's refining operations, even if the G7 action eventually pushes prices down later in the quarter.
